cards.text: Friend, grab an apron, because this chapter opens with more proverbs of Solomon, king of Israel. But this batch reached us through somebody else's hands. Somebody sat down and copied every single line.

cards.question: These proverbs of Solomon were copied down. Who copied them?

answers.text: The men of Hezekiah king of Judah
The men of Josiah king of Judah
The men of Jehoshaphat king of Judah

cards.text: Every line copied by hand, and I can't even copy a recipe card without getting dough ALL over it. First saying: God's glory is to conceal a matter, and kings get a kind of glory too.

cards.question: God's glory is to conceal a matter. What does Solomon say the glory of kings is?

cards.text: So kings dig into everything. Then Solomon points up at the high heavens and down into the deep earth, and says something about kings is just as far out of reach.

cards.question: What about kings does Solomon say cannot be searched?

cards.text: Next, a silversmith: “Remove the dross from the silver, and a vessel for a silversmith will come forth.” Get the junk out and something useful shows up, and friend, I know a LITTLE something about getting pulled out of the junk.

cards.question: Solomon says to remove the dross from the silver. Then he takes that idea to the king's court: remove the ___ from the king's presence.
Solomon says once the wicked are removed from the king's presence, his throne will be established in righteousness.

cards.text: Now some advice for walking into the king's court. Don't exalt yourself in front of the king, and don't go stand where the great men stand.

cards.question: Solomon says don't exalt yourself before the king or stand where the great men stand. He says it's better to be told “Come up here!” than to be what?

answers.text: Demoted in front of the prince
Ignored in front of the crowd
Questioned in front of the judges

cards.text: It's like grabbing the big chair at the head of the meeting table on your first day, and then the CEO walks in and just… stands there… looking at you. Next: even what you've seen with your own eyes, don't rush it to court.

cards.question: Solomon warns that if you rush to court, your neighbor may end up putting you to shame.

cards.text: So you and your neighbor have a dispute. Solomon says go ahead and argue your case with him, but he has a warning.

cards.question: Solomon says it's fine to spill someone else's secret if it helps you win the argument with your neighbor.

cards.text: Spill it, and whoever hears you can bring shame on you, and that bad name never goes away. That's the screenshot in the group chat that outlives us ALL.
Okay, friend, next picture: apples of gold in settings of silver, every piece sitting right where it belongs.

cards.question: Solomon says something is like apples of gold in settings of silver. What is it?

cards.text: More gold: an earring of gold, an ornament of fine gold. And jewelry doesn't do a thing sitting in the box. Somebody has to actually wear it.

cards.question: Solomon says a wise man's rebuke is like gold jewelry to a ___ ear.

cards.text: Now picture the cold of snow in the time of harvest. You've been out working the fields, and then that cool hits you like the AC kicking on halfway through a long summer drive.

cards.question: Solomon says a trustworthy messenger is like the cold of snow in the time of harvest to the people who send him.

cards.text: A good messenger refreshes the soul of his masters. Then the opposite: clouds and wind and not one drop of rain, like a tracker that says “Out for delivery” all day and then… NOTHING.

cards.question: Who does Solomon say is like clouds and wind without rain?

answers.text: The man who boasts of gifts never given
The man who hides his silver in the ground
The man who sleeps through the harvest

cards.text: Next, Solomon says through patience a ruler can be persuaded. Then he talks about a gentle tongue.

cards.question: Solomon says a gentle tongue is too weak to change anything.

cards.text: Weak? Friend, a gentle tongue can break a BONE. Next, Solomon says if you find honey, eat just what you need.

cards.question: What happens if you eat too much honey, according to Solomon?

cards.text: That's me and the cookie jar at midnight, and I've learned that lesson more times than I'm willing to admit. Solomon takes the same idea next door: seldom set foot in your neighbor's house.

cards.question: Solomon says the more often you visit your neighbor's house, the more he'll love you.

cards.text: Nope, he'll grow weary and hate you, like the guest still on the couch while the host is turning off the lights. Next, three weapons: a club, a sword and a sharp arrow.

cards.question: Who does Solomon say is like a club or a sword or a sharp arrow?

answers.text: A man who bears false witness against his neighbor
A man who moves his neighbor's boundary stone
A man who borrows and never pays it back

cards.text: Now picture biting down on a broken tooth, or putting weight on a foot out of joint, right when you need it most.

cards.question: Solomon says putting your confidence in a ___ man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint.

cards.text: Then picture someone taking off a garment on a cold day, or vinegar poured on a wound. OUCH, both of them.

cards.question: Solomon says someone is like taking off a garment on a cold day, or vinegar poured on a wound, when he does something to a heavy heart. What does he do?

cards.text: Now Solomon gets personal. Picture your enemy, and he's hungry.

cards.question: What does Solomon tell you to do for a hungry enemy?

cards.text: And if he's thirsty, give him water to drink. Solomon says doing that heaps burning coals on his head.

cards.question: Solomon adds one more thing about caring for your enemy. The ___ will reward you.

cards.text: I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, friend, and grudges take up way too much room. Next, weather: the north wind brings forth rain.

cards.question: As the north wind brings rain, Solomon says a backbiting tongue brings angry ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon names a spot most of us wouldn't pick to live: a corner of the roof. Not even the whole roof, just a CORNER, you and the gutters.

cards.question: What does Solomon say living on a corner of the roof is better than?

answers.text: Sharing a house with a quarrelsome wife
Living in a tent in the desert

cards.text: Now some relief: cold water to a weary soul. Solomon says something feels just like that.

cards.question: Solomon says good news from a distant land is like cold water to a weary soul.

cards.text: But water can go bad too. Picture a muddied spring or a polluted well.

cards.question: Solomon says a righteous man who stands up to the wicked is like a muddied spring.

cards.text: It's the righteous man who GIVES WAY to the wicked who's like a muddied spring or a polluted well. Then the honey comes back: it's not good to eat too much of it.

cards.question: Solomon sets something right next to eating too much honey. What else does he say is not good?

cards.text: That's checking how many likes your post got every thirty seconds, like it's gonna change if you just stare HARDER. Last picture: a city whose walls are broken down.

cards.question: Solomon says a man who does not control his ___ is like a city whose walls are broken down.

findings.problem: The card calls Solomon 'king of Israel.' That fact does not come from Proverbs 25:1, and the card cites only Proverbs 25:1, so the outside fact has no reference. Proverbs 1:1 is one source that gives it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'So kings dig into everything' stretches verse 2, which says only that it is the glory of kings to search out a matter. This line is a retelling, not one of Papa Dorin's jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'More gold: an earring of gold, an ornament of fine gold.' / 'And jewelry doesn't do a thing sitting in the box.' / 'Somebody has to actually wear it.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Then the opposite' tells the baker how verses 13 and 14 connect. The text never says verse 14 is the opposite of verse 13. Verse 14 is about a man who boasts of gifts never given, not about a messenger. The card also calls the messenger 'good' when verse 13 calls him 'trustworthy.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Weak?' / 'Friend, a gentle tongue can break a BONE.' / 'Next, Solomon says if you find honey, eat just what you need.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next word after 'angry' (looks, tears or crowds). Nothing in the setup lets the baker reason out 'looks' over the other two, so the card tests the wording of the line, not its meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
